topic: music chart rules on bundles, bulk purchases and chart methodology changes
statement: Chart compilers publish rules that bar purchases or streams made other than as genuine consumer transactions, and they revise their methodology on bundles: the UK Official Charts Company's album rules list prohibited activity and allow removal of irregular transactions, and in 2020 Billboard changed how albums sold with merchandise or tickets are counted.
scope: general; rules differ by compiler and country and change over time

sources.title: Official UK Album Chart Rules (January 2023)
sources.quote: purchasing albums or causing albums to be purchased or streamed other than as a genuine consumer transaction

sources.title: Billboard announces new chart rules, putting an end to ticket and merch bundles | Official Charts
sources.publisher: Official Charts Company (news report on Billboard rule change)
sources.quote: Bundles where the album is included as part of a "baked-in, single price option" will no longer be counted towards the charts.

notes: Cited a rule change announced by a compiler, via the UK compiler's news report; no named artist cited.

topic: streaming manipulation: purchased streams, followers and reviews
statement: Artificially inflated streams, including streams bought from third-party services or generated by bots and scripts, are recognised as a problem by streaming platforms, which state that such streams dilute the royalty pool and that paid stream-guarantee services violate their terms. The wider category of purchased followers and reviews is not covered by these sources.
scope: general; platform policies differ and change

sources.title: Artificial Streaming - Spotify for Artists
sources.quote: artificial streams dilute the royalty pool, shifting revenue from legitimate artists to bad actors.

sources.title: Artificial streaming and paid 3rd-party services that guarantee streams - Spotify
sources.quote: 3rd-party promotional services that advertise streams in return for payment violate our terms & conditions

sources.title: FBI Issues Warning: Cybercriminals Are Targeting Musicians
sources.publisher: Hypebot (trade press, reporting on an FBI warning)
sources.quote: Scammers are using AI-generated songs and automated bot networks to manipulate streaming numbers

notes: Platform documentation counts as a source for how the platform treats the practice; extent of fraud not asserted. Purchased followers and reviews not separately sourced, so statement scope is streams only.

topic: impersonation of scouts, A&R, managers and music-industry advance-fee scams
statement: Impersonation of label executives and scouts, and advance-fee or fake-contract approaches to artists, are described by an industry body and by trade press reporting on an FBI warning as an existing risk for emerging artists. These approaches are typically made through social media or email.
scope: general; no figure or named case relied on

sources.title: American Songwriter OP-ED by RIAA President & COO Michele Ballantyne: Shutting Down Fraudsters Who Prey on Artists' Hopes and Dreams
sources.quote: scammers pretending to be label executives and dangling false promises of a record deal to bait young artists

sources.title: FBI Issues Warning: Cybercriminals Are Targeting Musicians
sources.publisher: Hypebot (trade press, reporting on an FBI warning)
sources.quote: Industry professionals reported being contacted for fake record label contracts, collaborations, or promotional opportunities designed to steal sensitive data or "advance fees."

notes: The primary FBI notice was not retrieved; the trade-press report is cited as reporting it. Named cases in the op-ed deliberately not used.

topic: long-running online investment and romance fraud
statement: Government agencies describe investment frauds in which a person met online builds trust over weeks or months and then directs the victim to a fake trading website or app that displays growing returns, with withdrawals blocked by demands for further fees.

sources.title: Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) | Cryptocurrency Investment Schemes
sources.quote: The fake websites/apps allow the victims to track their investments and give the impression they are growing exponentially.

sources.title: Customer Advisory: Avoid Forex, Precious Metals, and Digital Asset Romance Scams | CFTC
sources.quote: even if the relationship has been building for weeks or months
